title: Providence and the Creative Hands of God
english: He says that the tyrannical rule of the devil is a throne of unrighteousness, by which they cruelly hunt the soul of the righteous, even as judges and arbitrators happen to condemn the innocent. For the devil's lust for evil is so great that it is equal to this wretchedness. For the Scripture calls him destruction instead of the Law-giver and perdition instead of the one who was lost; one place saying concerning him, 'Destruction came' (in this way also Judas was branded a son of perdition, having become a son of Satan), and another place calling him lawlessness; for it says his children have become sons of lawlessness, as it says concerning Christ, 'And son of lawlessness he shall not add to harm him.' Those who practice evil are his retainers, concerning whom it is said, 'Who shall rise up against me against evildoers?' or 'Who shall stand with me against those working lawlessness?' Both demons and evil men are such, acting through cunning the things foretold against the innocent and the righteous (Ps 94:1b–2).

They urge confession concerning those on whom they have acted wickedly, or concerning those who have suffered well from God, thanking Him who appeared and shone upon them, his countenance being the exact imprint of his hypostasis. For He is the image of the invisible God. It is possible for the third verse to correspond to the first and the fourth to the second, regarding those who rejoice in the Lord: 'We have seen your face in confession, but also we shout for joy to our Savior God in psalms.' For through psalms they shout for joy to the Lord, through which deeds they perform such things as are pleasing to Him; for the voice of the psalm submits such a thing.

The Scripture calls angels 'gods' (Ps 94:3b). But the Word of God has come to reign over those who have become gods. Wandering over all the earth, the Word, according to the account of providence, holds the things said of the ends of the earth in his hand; for his grasping is the ends of the earth, as he holds the ends of the earth. Since parts of the earth and its mountains belong to the Lord (and these are high in these matters), it should be noted that throughout all Scripture, the doctrine of those describing [the earth] up to the moon is refuted.

He sees providence. For it is said that He does not merely hold the ends of the earth there, but also in many places, indeed, as if He is Lord of both heaven and earth: 'I will confess to You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth.'

Regarding thought, they come into the hand of God, for only those who are further than the ends of the earth by wisdom and citizenship are under His protective and almighty hand; thus no one is able to snatch them away, those who are in the hand of the Father and in the hand of the Son. These ends, by way of thought, are the sheep of Christ, concerning whom the Lord says: 'My sheep hear my voice, and I give them eternal life' (John 10:27), and furthermore: 'and no one shall snatch them from my hand' (John 10:28); and no one is able to snatch them from the hand of my Father (John 10:29). Since the interpreted ends of the earth are in the hand of God, it is fitting that He also attains the heights of the mountains, seeing those men who are separated by life and godly wisdom. But they are exceptional, surpassing even the heights of the mountains which He spoke of; perhaps they are the ends of the earth, the men walking upon the earth, yet having their citizenship and their heart in heaven because they have stored up treasure there, seeing the high angels as their wealth.

It is to be noted that the dry land is said to be formed not by one hand but by hands, just as 'the heavens are the work of your hands' (Ps 94:4) and 'your hands made me and fashioned me' (Ps 94:5). But as to what these creative hands are, it is a matter of perplexity; for one is, as we confess, the active hand of God, the Word of God, but with this hand another is also coordinated through many Scriptures, being itself creative. And it is pleasing to say, having become a follower of divine men and the apostles, that the creative hands of God are the Only-begotten and the Holy Spirit. This was the opinion of Irenaeus most especially, from which it is evident that the position being set forth is an ancient glory, not merely a passive one, but a creative one, and the Holy Spirit is creative.

They call upon one another to worship God, not by going from one place to another. For it is no longer a local worship, as was the case when Jerusalem and the temple there were established. For they worship the Lord, according to the prophet,

title: The Temple of God and the Restoration of the Soul
english: Each one [comes] from his own place, not sensorially and bodily but in spirit and truth. Therefore, those who worship and fall down to him, bowing the knee to him and confessing him, come according to a disposition rather than a change of place; not only those on earth but also those in heavens and under the earth, weeping before him the weeping of repentance, and how much some weep and suffer. But a blameless weeping, escaping every stain, becomes [one who] is confident before the Lord.

And they say the reason by which the things written are fulfilled, asserting that he himself is our God and we are sheep of his pasture, a relationship of the people to God being shown through this word. Because of this he says: We become the people of his pasture, which he himself granted to make himself our God; for since he himself is our God, and we become the people of his pasture, and since we are the people of his pasture, he is our God. And being the people of his pasture, we are also sheep of his hand, he being our shepherd. Therefore no one shall snatch us from his right hand; for I myself give them eternal life, and no one shall snatch them from my hand (Ps 94:7c–9).

Having said that these words were spoken by the Holy Spirit as the end of the psalm, the apostle placed them in the Epistle to the Hebrews somewhat randomly and brought an interpretation to them. But he interpreted 'today', referring to the age that has fully come; for each day of the age is signified by 'today'. But the heart is hardened, appearing hard and contrary through all sin, bowing down to wickedness like that of Pharaoh. Therefore, abandoning this hardness, let us bow our hearing to the shouting God in order to become righteous.

Another says 'I said, I provided food' (Ps 94:10-11), [referring to] not every generation, but that generation always associating with error because of not wanting the knowledge of God; he says that God, having been angered, swore not to enter into his rest, saying these things in Psalm 106. Having explained this word of Paul, we will say nothing more than what was said then. Understand also thus: the rational soul, becoming according to the image and likeness of God, is the [intellect] of the one who has been made, especially with virtue...

Being [sinful], the one sinning is taken captive and is disgraced, so that he is no longer a temple of God. For if God says concerning some, 'My spirit shall by no means remain in these men because they are flesh' (cf. Psalm 51:11), for formerly, when the temple of the divine Spirit was dwelling in them, it was like His own; but those sinning have become flesh, subject to passion and material, having taken [it] on, the one dwelling in them has departed as a conqueror, and they remained under destruction by the evil spirits who captured them.

Therefore, just as the one sinning, having become a captive, ceases to be a temple of God through the destruction of his edifice built of virtues, so also the one returning to God through repentance is not only ransomed from captivity, but is also founded and built up as a temple of God through correctness of mind and excellent deeds. And this is what the introductory part of the psalm declares. For after the captivity, once the temple is built, a gracious song of thanksgiving is sent up for the forgiveness of the captivity and the dedication of the temple.

And regarding the literal sense, one will be able to take what is according to the place. For it appears that the temple was built in the times of Ezra after the captivity. It must be said that concerning such a thing, David, having seen more prophetically the ancient restoration of the temple, has made the song for the dedication of the temple. But the singers, having put off the old man and having put on the new, being renewed into becoming according to the image of the one who created him, and being made suitable to the new discipleship of the new covenant, conforming to the newness of the teaching of Christ, [sing].

Here indeed all the earth is commanded to obey, and in [the heavens] to worship: 'Let all the earth worship you and sing to you' (Psalm 95:6); and it is said in Isaiah, 'The whole earth is full of His greatness' (Isaiah 6:3), and in others, 'The whole earth is full of His glory.' Not all who sing to God are commanded to obey Him and to bless His name. For through good works and knowledge of the truth, one blesses and glorifies the name of God. For it is said in the Gospel, 'Let your light shine before men' (Matthew 5:16), so that they may see your good works and glorify [the Father].
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Two Covenants and the Proclamation of Glory
english: your Father who is in the heavens. For when the approach of God has been called to us, doing all things according to the right reason, we bless through blessing, we act or we bear the name of the Lord; for not otherwise having it, we pray that it itself might become blessed and holy.

But regarding precision, as it has been said about this in Psalm 22, 'Let us exalt his name to the same degree' (Ps 22:2); now we are satisfied with those things said through brevity. Strive as much as possible and in this way to receive the set-forth words; those who offer up to the Old Testament things happening in place of sensible things offer an old hymn. For after the Pharaoh, the tyrant of Egypt, was submerged, Moses, with all the Hebrew multitude, sang a hymn: 'Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously glorified' (Ps 95:2-3); he cast horse and rider into the sea. And regarding other things having happened, it is more bodily to see the hymn of Israel in the Pentateuch and the rest of the Old Scripture.

But those who depart from the antiquity of the letter to be discipled by the novelty of the Spirit, being made upright intellectually and spiritually, offer a new hymn to the Lord, the power of which having been abolished, the death of the devil having been overcome, and the underground realm of the mental Egypt having become submerged, Jesus, through the grace of God, having tasted every death. And those having sung to the Lord, not having been freed from all curses but having received the blessing supplied from God, bless the name of him who blessed them with all spiritual blessing in the heavenly places.

The set-forth commands become for the disciples of Jesus who hear: 'Go and make disciples of all nations' (Matt 28:19). For the Holy Spirit wills to accomplish the evangelical work in them with a swift and undivided zeal. For this 'day by day' presents to them the continuous evangelizing of the salvation of God, concerning which it has been said: 'This is truly the Savior of the world' (John 4:42), and again, 'A Savior has been born to you today, who is Christ the Lord' (Luke 2:11). For the prophecy saying 'All flesh shall see the salvation of God' (Luke 24:46), as the apostles evangelize his salvation day by day, shall reach its fulfillment.

It is possible to take the two covenants of the Savior, who is the sun of righteousness, from day to day. Since those who are commanded to evangelize are law-abiding and have the light of the first day, they subsequently follow that day with another day according to the new covenant, being enlightened, and they proclaim the salvation of God. Proclaiming Christ the Savior, who is the salvation of God, they announce to all nations the glory of God, which is Christ, who happens to be the radiance of the glory of God; concerning this, it is written in Isaiah: 'The glory of God shall be seen' (Isa 60:1), and also, 'And the glory of God shall rise upon you' (Isa 60:1). For just as Christ is the wisdom and power and truth and righteousness of God, so also his glory is.

Moreover, they are commanded to announce his wonders to all peoples, concerning which it is said to God in Psalm 76: 'You have done many things, Lord my God, your wonderful works' (Ps 76:6). The prophet Isaiah says that the cause of these wonders is: 'Lord my God, I will glorify you, I will sing praise to your name, for you have done wonderful things, a true ancient purpose' (Isa 25:1). For Christ the Savior has done wonderful things, having freed every soul suffering under the devil, establishing the ancient purpose of God, according to which man existed as being straight, having come to be in the image and likeness of the Creator. And if you wish the things being proclaimed to the people to be wonderful, immense powers, such as Jesus raising the dead and restoring the blind to sight, and if anything else of this kind is written, you do not err. And it is also possible to do so: manifest through theology the most unclouded knowledge concerning God, so that the nations might have right discourse concerning God, being freed from much-godly fear. These things will in no way suit those returning from Babylon in the times of Cyrus or in the times of Darius, who perceptibly built the [temple] while Zerubbabel and Joshua the priest were presiding over the building in Judah after the captivity. For these things are fulfilled through works after the presence of our Savior, with all his disciples wandering through the whole earth and evangelizing, having announced his salvation to all.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
